subject: Theranos Edison blood testing device clinical accuracy claims
executive_summary: Theranos claimed its Edison device could perform hundreds of tests from a single finger prick, but independent studies and CMS reports show high failure rates and inaccurate results, disproving the device’s clinical accuracy claims.
key_findings: Edison device failed 87% of hormone QC tests and 22% PSA tests in 2015.
Independent study found 12.2% out-of-range results vs 8.3% LabCorp, 7.5% Quest.
evidence_synthesis: Multiple independent sources confirm that Theranos’ Edison device did not deliver on its promised clinical accuracy. A CMS report (2015) documented an 87% failure rate for hormone QC tests and a 22% failure rate for PSA, indicating severe unreliability. An independent Journal of Clinical Investigation study reported that the device rejected 2.2% of samples and produced 12.2% out‑of‑range results, higher than competitors LabCorp (8.3%) and Quest (7.5%). Together, these findings provide strong evidence that the Edison device’s accuracy claims are false.
conflict_resolution_notes: No conflicting evidence found; all sources refute claims.
